turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Observations are in. Blood pressure is one eighteen over seventy-two, oxygen sats 98 percent. Pulse was ninety-two... no, sorry, one hundred and eight.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right. Miss Hale. Tired, are you?
[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): Yes, Doctor. I have been unusually tired, and I become breathless on the stairs.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): How long?
[SEG0005] person_3 (PATIENT): Err, about three weeks. Forgive me, that is not right. It is nearer two months.
[SEG0006] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I'm her mum. She nods off on the sofa the minute she's home. We missed the earlier bus as well, absolute chaos on the ring road.
[SEG0007] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any fever?
[SEG0008] person_3 (PATIENT): No, Doctor. I have not had a fever.
[SEG0009] person_2 (DOCTOR): Cough?
[SEG0010] person_3 (PATIENT): I have been craving ice, quite a lot of it. It is rather odd, and I am a little embarrassed to say so.
[SEG0011] person_2 (DOCTOR): Mm. Any cough?
[SEG0012] person_3 (PATIENT): No, Doctor. There is no cough.
[SEG0013] person_2 (DOCTOR): Weight up or down?
[SEG0014] person_3 (PATIENT): I am not certain, Doctor. Perhaps my skirts are a little looser, but I could not tell you when that began. I do not weigh myself.
[SEG0015] person_2 (DOCTOR): Periods heavy?
[SEG0016] person_3 (PATIENT): No. They are quite normal, regular, and not at all heavy.
[SEG0017] person_2 (DOCTOR): What do you take?

[SEG0018] person_3 (PATIENT): I take amlodopine for the pressure, five milligrams... no, ten milligrams, every morning. The cholesterol one at night, atorvastatin twenty milligrams, for my cholesterol. Metforman, the sugar tablets, five hundred milligrams twice a day. And only the Ayurvedic powder in the morning.
[SEG0019] person_2 (DOCTOR): Strict vegetarian?
[SEG0020] person_3 (PATIENT): Yes, Doctor. I eat no meat, no fish and no eggs. I have kept to that for years.
[SEG0021] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I do her meals separate. She won't have so much as an egg in a cake. I picked up that powder at the chemist, though I couldn't tell you what's in it.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): You're pale. Chest is clear, no wheeze. Pulse is rapid. Heart sounds otherwise normal.
[SEG0023] person_2 (DOCTOR): Likely low iron. Provisional only. The ice and the stairs fit that. Bloods will settle it.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): Full blood count, ferritin and a B12, booked for today. Come back in two weeks.
[SEG0025] person_3 (PATIENT): Ought I to change what I eat whilst we wait, Doctor?
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): Lentils, dark green veg, orange juice alongside. No iron tablets until the numbers are back.
[SEG0027] person_1 (NURSE): I'll book those bloods at the desk for this afternoon.
[SEG0028] person_3 (PATIENT): Thank you, Doctor. I am very grateful.
[SEG0029] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): We'll go straight down. She always loses the little tickets, but that's by the by.
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): Fine. Fortnight, for the results. Off you go.

spec.situation: Tired young woman, strict vegetarian, breathless on stairs, craving ice; periods normal by her account; blood tests planned; diet advice.

traps.happens: The doctor asks only two to four review-of-systems questions (for example fever, weight, cough). Several other body systems are never asked about. One of the asked questions gets a vague or mixed answer.
traps.label_rule: negative_findings / review_of_systems ONLY for items the doctor actually asked AND the patient answered, evidence = that question and answer. Never add review-of-systems entries for systems nobody asked about, and never cite an unrelated turn (for example a turn about tiredness) for a system review.

traps.happens: The patient lists medicines with their purpose ('amlodipine for the pressure', 'the cholesterol one at night', 'sugar tablets') and also mentions a herbal or shop remedy in passing ('only the Ayurvedic powder in the morning'). Their chronic conditions are never asked about directly.
traps.label_rule: Each medicine is recorded with the dose and timing said for THAT medicine; the herbal remedy is a medicine too (currently_used). A condition the patient states through its medicine ('for the pressure') is a past_medical_history entry ONLY if the patient actually said the condition name or its everyday name ('the pressure' = hypertension, normalized); do not invent a duration.

features: patient_answers_other_question: the patient answers a different question than the one asked, and the doctor repeats or lets it go.
self_correction: a speaker states a number, drug name or duration and then corrects it in the same turn or later ('seventy-five... no, hundred and fifty'). The label holds only the corrected value.
